narrative.summary: The AI-governance instruments identified so far in Bahrain are led by the Information & eGovernment Authority (iGA) under the Ministerial Committee for Information and Communication Technology. The main instrument is the General Policy for the Use of AI (2025), which binds all government entities and was launched alongside Bahrain's adoption of the GCC Guiding Manual on AI Ethics. The judiciary has its own AI rules in the 2026 edition of the Supreme Judicial Council's code of conduct, and the Personal Data Protection Law (2018) applies to personal data used in AI systems. No national AI strategy has been found. A government bill regulating AI technologies and systems, prepared on a 2024 Shura Council proposal, has been before the Council of Representatives since November 2024.
lead_institutions: Ministerial Committee for Information and Communication Technology
narrative.review_notes: Reviewed on 6 October 2026 and rechecked on 18 October 2026: the Central Bank of Bahrain rulebook and the National Cyber Security Center were searched and no AI-specific rules or guidance were found, though the central bank's rules on automated investment advice and the cyber centre's AI awareness campaign are held for review; the UNESCO readiness assessment is now listed as background rather than a government document. The AI bill is still with parliament, with no 2026 step found in parliamentary records.

instruments.english_title: General Policy for the Use of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 dated 20 May 2025, approved by the Ministerial Committee for Information and Communication Technology; launched 27 July 2025 together with Bahrain's adoption of the GCC Guiding Manual on AI Ethics.
instruments.summary: Requires all Bahraini government entities to comply with its rules and principles when using AI. They must align AI use with personal data, cybersecurity and open-data rules, keep human oversight, audit AI use regularly, assign accountability to people rather than systems, and build staff awareness.

instruments.official_title: Law No. (30) of 2018 with Respect to Personal Data Protection Law
instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 30 of 2018)
instruments.current_status: In force; supervised by the Personal Data Protection Authority. Promulgated at Riffa Palace on 28 Shawwal 1439 AH, corresponding to 12 July 2018, and published in Official Gazette issue No. 3375 of Thursday 19 July 2018. Under its Fourth Article it takes effect from the first day of the month following one year after publication in the Official Gazette, that is 1 August 2019.
instruments.summary: Bahrain's general personal data law. It sets conditions for lawful processing, data-subject rights and controller duties, and governs personal data used in AI systems. Enforced by the Personal Data Protection Authority.

instruments.english_title: Code of Conduct for the Members of the Judiciary (2026 Edition), including the Guidelines on the Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems in Judicial Work
instruments.current_status: The Code was adopted by the Supreme Judicial Council in February 2024; the 2026 Edition, issued in February 2026 (per its own '2026 Edition' note), added the Seventeenth provision, 'Guidelines on the Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems in Judicial Work'. Arabic and English texts are linked from the Council's home page. The Code calls itself a guiding instrument, but the AI provision is written as prohibitions binding on members of the judiciary; legal-status classification may need review. No exact day of issue is stated. Classed mandatory-in-scope: binding on members of the judiciary and the Public Prosecution only (PROTOCOL §3 court rule).
instruments.summary: The 2026 Edition of the Supreme Judicial Council's code of conduct for judges and other members of the judiciary adds AI guidelines (Seventeenth provision). They confine AI systems to 'supporting tasks' such as legal research, data analysis, drafting help and statistics; prohibit issuing judgments, decisions or any judicial or Public Prosecution act in reliance on AI; and require members to verify outputs, avoid biased or fabricating systems, never enter personal data into AI systems, anonymise case data used for training, and respect intellectual property. It requires AI training for members and provides for a Council working group to oversee judicial AI use and propose detailed instructions and updates.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Bahraini judiciary's own binding-style rules for AI use by judges and prosecutors (sectoral, public-sector, ethics, generative-ai).

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: The government and the national ministries were searched. No AI-specific material was found at the central bank or the National Cyber Security Center, or for standards, procurement and regulatory sandboxes, and most ministries had no AI document of their own. AI material of the Public Prosecution and the Higher Education Council remains to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): Deep review completed on 6 October 2026. The national government portal could not be read automatically; the AI policy record follows the final version published by the Information & eGovernment Authority. The Central Bank of Bahrain, the National Cyber Security Center and the standards and procurement bodies were searched, and no AI-specific material was found. The GCC guiding manual on AI ethics applies through the GCC regional layer.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-06. bahrain.bh blocks automated reading; the AI policy record now points to the iGA final version (30 July 2025). Searched with no AI-specific material found: Central Bank of Bahrain rulebook, National Cyber Security Center, standards, procurement, sandbox. The GCC Guiding Manual on AI Ethics is held in the GCC regional file and applies here automatically. Ministry catch-up 2026-10-13 (PROTOCOL §2 ministry rule, applied after this country's deep review; one agent, 30 minutes, national ministries' own AI documents only, nothing else re-reviewed): 1 record(s) added. Ministries: Supreme Judicial Council (judiciary, incl. Public Prosecution members): Code of Conduct for the Members of the Judiciary, 2026 Edition, with Guidelines on the Use of AI Systems in Judicial Work, Feb 2026 (recorded). Ministry of Justice, Islamic Affairs and Waqf: home page and searches, nothing found. Public Prosecution: site unreachable; only news of a proposed GCC model framework and an internal AI team (lead). Ministry of Education: home page and linked PDFs (student discipline regulation 2025, Private Educational Institutions Law 2026) checked, no AI document; AI education platform/curriculum items are projects only. Higher Education Council: site unreachable; nothing found by search; University of Bahrain AI Usage Regulation noted (lead, institution-level). Ministry of Health: home page and Health Improvement Strategy 2023-2026 checked (no AI content); nothing found. NHRA (regulator) not re-reviewed. Ministry of Interior: home page and searches, nothing found (chairs the ICT ministerial committee behind the recorded iGA policy). Bahrain Defence Force: nothing found. Ministry of Foreign Affairs: site blocked (405), nothing found by search. Ministry of Finance and National Economy / National Bureau for Revenue / Customs: nothing found. Ministry of Labour / Social Insurance Organization: nothing found. Ministry of Transportation and Telecommunications: Telecommunications, ICT and Digital Economy Sector Strategy 2022-2026 mentions AI only in passing (not recorded); nothing else found. Ministry of Industry and Commerce: nothing found. Ministry of Information Affairs: site blocked (405); AI-made TV content only, no guidance found. Other ministries (Oil and Environment, Tourism, Works, Housing, Social Development, Youth): nothing found in combined searches. Civil Service Bureau: home page and searches, nothing found; public-servant AI rules are the already-recorded iGA General Policy.. Not reached: Public Prosecution website (ppo.gov.bh, DNS/proxy failure); Higher Education Council website (hec.gov.bh, proxy 502); Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Information Affairs websites (HTTP 405 to curl; covered by search only). Could not verify: Public Prosecution AI framework proposal and AI team (news only; ppo.gov.bh unreachable).; Higher Education Council AI guidance (hec.gov.bh unreachable; none found by search)..

Gulf benchmark 2026-10-18: (1) CBB: cbb.gov.bh links its Rulebook to cbben.thomsonreuters.com (confirmed from the CBB home page). Rulebook full-text searches (current versions) returned no hits for 'artificial intelligence' or 'machine learning'; 'artificial'/'intelligence' hits are unrelated (market abuse, capital deductions, STR/cyber intelligence). 'algorithm' leads to Module DA Digital Financial Advice, DA-2 Algorithm Governance (Added April 2019; design documentation, bias/error controls, testing) - not AI-labelled, held as a lead. CBB site search for AI shows only news (31 Aug 2026 CBB-NCSC awareness event 'Securing Financial Services Data in the AI Era'; GCC capital-markets committee study on AI, 7 Sep 2026). NCSC: Standards & Controls (Baseline Cyber Security Controls, policy templates, Cyber Trust Program, RMF, CNI controls, incident response plan), Executive Decision No. 36 of 2026 (19-08-2026, cyber standards for critical sectors; no AI text), Best Practices (4 items, none AI) and the National Cyber Security Strategy 2025-2028 summary (AI mentioned only in passing) checked; the 'Be Smarter Than AI' awareness campaign and newsletters held as a lead. No AI-specific CBB or NCSC instrument found. (2) UNESCO RAM report i-d71e94bec8cd moved to leads (UNESCO methodology assessment, ADG foreword; not a government instrument); instrument, its source s-e4436d7a7b28 removed after the lead was added; its organisation entry o-1d93ca60dcaa deleted 2026-10-18 (approved); the two history entries kept. index-readiness moved to no-material. (3) AI bill: nuwab.bh records 26 Nov 2024 (bill received), 24 Feb 2025 (committee postponed), 21 Apr 2025 (committee review with Nasser Centre); no 2026 record found. shura.bh is a JavaScript app whose legislative search needs an API key embedded in the site; not used. GDN (11 Oct 2026) reports the bill still under debate (news only). (4) PDPL: issue date 12 July 2018 (28 Shawwal 1439) read on the PDP Authority PDF and lloc.gov.bh; Gazette No. 3375, 19 July 2018 (iGA-hosted Gazette extract); effective 1 August 2019 derived from Article 4. legalaffairs.gov.bh home page reachable only via headless browser; law text taken from lloc.gov.bh.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (coverage_audit.no_material_found_note): The Public Prosecution and Higher Education Council sites were unavailable, so their AI material remains to be checked.

leads.note: Proposal approved by the Shura Council on 28 April 2024 and referred to the government for drafting. Council of Representatives records (nuwab.bh): on 26 November 2024 (8th ordinary sitting, 3rd session, 6th legislative term) the House received the Prime Minister's letter on the draft law 'بتنظيم تقنيات وأنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي واستخداماته' prepared on the Shura proposal, for referral to the Legislative and Legal Affairs Committee; on 24 February 2025 the committee postponed it for further study; on 21 April 2025 the committee reviewed it with the Sheikh Nasser Scientific and Technical Centre. Update 2026-10-18: no 2026 committee report, plenary vote or Shura second reading found in nuwab.bh records; the shura.bh legislative database could not be queried automatically. Press reports in October 2026 describe the bill as still under debate. Record as a draft once official text is published.
